stories.headline: Chhattisgarh government declares school holiday amid heavy rain, flood-like situation
stories.title: Chhattisgarh government declares school holiday amid heavy rain, flood-like situation
stories.summary: Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai ordered relief and rescue operations across the State after incessant rain inundated low-lying areas and cut off villages in the Bastar region
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Chhattisgarh government has declared a holiday for schools across the State on Saturday (September 26, 2026), as heavy rain battered parts of the State, inundating several areas and cutting off villages.
Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai, in a post on X on Friday (September 25, 2026), announced the closure of all government, private and aided schools, saying the safety of students was the top priority.

Mr. Sai said heavy rainfall could lead to waterlogging, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and transportation difficulties in several areas, and that the decision was taken to ensure children faced no risk.

He also instructed District Collectors to conduct relief and rescue operations with full vigilance in view of flooding and waterlogging caused by continuous rainfall, including in the Bastar division, which comprises seven districts, another statement said.
"There should be no delay in providing assistance to people in need in affected areas.
Keeping the safety of citizens as the highest priority, the administration should remain prepared to deal with every situation," the release quoted Mr. Sai as saying.
He directed officials to monitor the situation, with special attention to villages and settlements in low-lying areas and those near rivers and streams.
Incessant heavy rain battered several parts of the State on Friday (September 25, 2026), inundating low-lying areas, swelling rivers and cutting off remote settlements in the Bastar region.

Mr. Sai asked relief and rescue teams to remain ready with the necessary resources, and directed district administrations, the police, urban local bodies, panchayats and other departments to work in coordination so that immediate assistance is provided in any emergency.

He also directed officials to ensure safe shelters, food, drinking water, medicines and other essential facilities as required, and asked people not to venture unnecessarily into waterlogged areas or swollen rivers and streams, and to follow the district administration's advisories.

A rain-related death was reported in Kondagaon district, where a farmer, 40, drowned on Friday (September 25, 2026) after falling into a flooded drain while trying to catch fish in a partially submerged paddy field, officials said.
Between June 1, 2026, and September 25, 2026, the State recorded an average of 1,082.4 mm of rainfall, which is 100.1% of its 10-year seasonal benchmark of 1,081.5 mm.

stories.title: Amend 2023 Election Commissioner appointment Act, says former Andhra CM YS Jagan

article_sentences: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links.

Against the backdrop of The Indian Express’ investigative report, former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy said that the Chief Election Commissioner Act of 2023 should be revisited.

The IE report had, among other things, stated that two Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised 14 objections pertaining to electoral roll revisions over the past 10 months and had disagreed with CEC Gyanesh Kumar on multiple counts.

Issuing a statement on Friday, September 25, YS Jagan said the public needs clarity on what objections were recorded, what action was taken and how transparently the system functioned – be it for adding, deleting or restoring names on electoral rolls.

“The very bill (Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 ) which had our support then, should be revisited now in the current background.
The Central government (Ruling Party) should come forward, set the normal in place dispelling this fear,” he added.
The 2023 Act sets the formal legal rules for how top election officials are chosen, paid, and managed in India.
Before the 2023 Act, the Supreme Court had ruled that the selection panel to appoint EC members should include the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India (CJI).
The 2023 Act changed this to include Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition and a Union Cabinet minister, making the appointment of Election Commission officials less neutral.

“An amendment to the bill be brought forward where the election commissioner is appointed by the three member committee which has Leader of Opposition (LoP), Chief Justice of India (CJI) and the Prime Minister as members once again,” Jagan said adding that this move would definitely regain the esteem and the confidence on Election Commission.
Jagan also said that this was important in the backdrop of the SIR process in Andhra Pradesh.

stories.headline: Arunachal Pradesh Congress Stages Dharna over Election Commission, SIR
stories.title: Arunachal Pradesh Congress Stages Dharna over Election Commission, SIR
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: ITANAGAR: The Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) joined the nationwide protest called by the Congress against the Election Commission on Friday, staging a peaceful dharna near Nirvachan Bhawan in Itanagar.

The party demanded the resignation and removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, a freeze on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and an independent inquiry into decisions concerning electoral rolls.
The APCC also sought criminal proceedings against Kumar and an investigation into the orders issued under his tenure.
It demanded that upcoming elections be put on hold and the electoral roll restored to the January 2025 voters' list until the completion of an independent inquiry.

The party further sought custody of all SIR-related files by the Supreme Court and repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of Election Commissioners, calling for new legislation with greater participation of civil society.
The Congress has cited reported differences among the three Election Commissioners over decisions and orders relating to the SIR as one of the reasons for seeking an independent review.
The Election Commission, however, maintained that differences of views were part of institutional deliberations and that its recent orders were taken unanimously.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Saturday questioned a change to the online voter registration process, alleging that the Election Commission had added a mandatory declaration to Form 6 without following the procedure required to amend it.

In a post on X, Ramesh said the online form was altered in early July to ask applicants whether their parents or grandparents had been included in an earlier Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
He called the change “totally illegal” and said it could make registration harder for young and first-time voters.
Ramesh contrasted the new requirement with the Election Commission’s direction to officials to organise special enrolment camps for young voters and publicise them on social media.
He argued that encouraging registration while adding a further condition to the online process was contradictory.
Citing the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, Ramesh said the power to amend Form 6 lay with the central government, not the Election Commission acting on its own.
He claimed that any change to the prescribed form would require an amendment to the rules and communication to Parliament.
The rules, including Form 6, are published by the government.

stories.summary: The Maharashtra government on Saturday declared 265 of the 358 talukas in the state as drought-affected, announcing relief measures, including restructuring of crop loans, concession in land revenue and deferment of recovery of agriculture-related loans. stories.title: Supreme Court orders sealing of over 16,000 properties, demolition of illegal structures in Meerut
stories.summary: A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan also formed a judicial commission, led by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, to conduct a thorough inquiry in Uldepur, on the outskirts of Meerut, regarding the nature of land where these illegal residential colonies have developed

article_sentences: Taking serious note of illegal constructions and the conversion of residential properties for commercial use, the Supreme Court has directed the Uttar Pradesh government to seal over 16,000 properties in Meerut and demolish unauthorised structures.

A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan also formed a judicial commission, led by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, to conduct a thorough inquiry in Uldepur, on the outskirts of Meerut, regarding the nature of land where these illegal residential colonies have developed.

"We are shocked and disturbed to learn, reading the status report, that hundreds of illegal residential colonies have come up at Uldepur," the Bench said, after perusing the report by P. Guruprasad, Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Awas Evam Vikas Parishad.
The Bench noted that the department has undertaken an inspection and survey of various parts of Meerut.
The report showed that the town has been divided into four zones: Zone-A, Zone-B, Zone-C, and Zone-D.
"In Zone-A, 16 teams deputed for the purpose of inspection/survey have identified 16,726 structures to be absolutely illegal/unauthorised.
Out of 16,726 structures, 12,907 comprise residential, 874 residential-cum-non- residential, and 2945 non-residential constructions," it noted in its September 21 order.

The top court, hearing a contempt petition related to non-compliance with previous directives on illegal constructions, instructed the authorities to take appropriate action against all the 16,726 illegal structures in Zone-A at the earliest.
"The first step in the process is to ask the occupants to vacate the premises and to seal all these premises, i.e., the 16,726 illegal structures.
We direct accordingly.
It is possible that some of these structures may be in a dilapidated condition and may collapse, resulting in casualties.
We do not want this to happen at any cost.

stories.title: Substance abuse among children is a child protection issue: CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday said substance abuse among children must be understood as a child protection issue, rather than as a matter of public health concern. Delivering the Pataliputra Pragya Pravah lecture on 'Childhood Beyond Drugs: Protection, Care and Reintegration' at the Bihar Lok Bhavan here, Justice Kant cited a recent Lancet study to say that at least one in five teenagers in India were at moderate to high risk of substance abuse. "Substance abuse among children must be understood not only as a matter of public health concern, but as a child protection issue as well," he said. Justice Kant stressed the need for a "child-sensitive response" to addiction to protect not only the child's physical and mental well-being but also their dignity and sense of self-worth. stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses BJP MLAs' Plea Challenging Quashing Of Corruption Complaint Against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (25 September) dismissed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) against the Karnataka High Court's judgment which had quashed criminal complaint against Karnataka's Energy Minister KJ George and Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) officials over alleged irregularities in the tender procurement and installation of smart electricity meters in Karnataka.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran declined to interfere with the High Court's order, holding that there existed “no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”

A criminal complaint was filed against Minister KJ George and BESCOM officials, by three MLAs (CN Ashwath Narayan, SR Vishwanath, and Dheeraj Muniraj) of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), alleging offences under Sections 314, 316, and 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), and Section 13(1)(a), 13(1)(b) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act), in connection with the tender for smart meters.
The MLAs had first approached the Lokayukta police before filing the complaint before the PC Act Special Court.

On George's petition seeking quashing of the proceedings, the Karnataka High Court had quashed the proceedings reasoning that it had found no material to substantiate the corruption allegation, and no allegation of any pecuniary benefit having been received by the Minister.
Aggrieved by the High Court's ruling, the BJP MLAs filed an SLP before the Supreme Court.
“Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and having gone through the materials on record, we find no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”
For Petitioners: Mr. Lakshmy Iyenger, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Dhawesh Pahuja, AOR; Mr. Saket Gogia, Adv.; Mr. Aakash Vt, Adv.; Mr. Harshith S, Adv.; Ms. Gauri Pande, Adv.; Mr. Mansingh, Adv.
Mr. Deepesh Meena, Adv.; Mr. Adithya KS, Adv.; Ms. Harshita Singh Tomar, Adv.
For Respondents: Mr. Kapil Sibal, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Vivek Jain, AOR; Ms. Suchitra Kumbhat, Adv.
Mr. Rohit H Nair, Adv.; Ms. Ishika Gandhi, Adv.; Mr. Shathabish Shivanna, Adv.; Mr. Abhishek Janardhan, Adv.; Mr. Samrudh Suraj Hegde, Adv.
